subject: QBR: scaling slots, short-burst plans & token-burn projection
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: scaling slots, short-burst plans & token-burn projection

Team —

I put together a tighter scenario matrix for the QBR focused specifically on (a) short-burst headroom for marketing spikes, (b) steady-state slot counts for Dedicated pools, and (c) token-level burn impact under our proposed batching+prefix-cache profile. See attached: capacity_scenarios_v2.xlsx and token_burn_model.csv.

Top asks for this week:
- Decision A: Accept 25% short-burst headroom vs. conservative 10%? (impacts capex/commit sizing)
- Decision B: Preferred quantization profile for the high-throughput pool (int8 vs q4f16 trade-offs we outline on tab 3)
- Decision C: SLO relaxation tolerance we can accept for aggressive batching (we modeled 0%, 5%, 10% latency windows)

Notes (high level):
- With the 25% burst headroom scenario, projected GPU spend increases ~18% but token cost/unit drops ~12% because batching efficiency rises.
- The token_burn_model uses last quarter's traffic shapes + a synthetic spike reflecting a new feature launch. If we tweak the prefix-cache hit rates from 60% -> 75% the unit cost improves materially (see sheet "cache-sensitivity").

Please review and add comments in the Drive doc (link below). Need your finals by EOD Tuesday so we can fold into the QBR one-pager.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-capacity-qbr-2027
Notion: https://www.notion.so/redwood/Capacity-Runway-Checklist-2027-07

Thanks —
Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_scenarios_v2.xlsx (xlsx), token_burn_model.csv (csv)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: scaling slots, short-burst plans & token-burn projection

Priyom —

Thanks for the concise matrix. I skimmed the file and the model assumptions look sane. A few high-level directives from the leadership side:
- Prioritize the 25% short-burst plan only if we can show a <1.5x worst-case month spend shock with a contractual cap (i.e., auto-throttle at commit threshold).
- For the QBR, synthesize a one-slide risk matrix that covers: procurement lag (3–6 weeks), vendor spot pricing volatility, and worst-case RU (request unit) growth.
- I prefer the q4f16 path for the high-throughput pool as the baseline; call out any regression risk with a short rollout window.

Also loop in Amanda (AWS) for immediate SKU/quote context — if we can secure a short-burst credit arrangement that changes the calculus.

Irene, Marcus — flag any red flags on the procurement timing and the rollout risk.

-L

Lauren Bishop
VP, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 3 Jul 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: scaling slots, short-burst plans & token-burn projection

Looping in quick data support — attached a short trace export and utilization overlays (gpu_utilization_trace.zip). Two operational notes: 

1) The aggressive batching profile shows latency tail risk for sequences >1024 tokens under 10% SLO relaxation; we should target experiments that validate the cache-hit distribution at that seq length before we finalize the rollout.
2) On Dedicated: we can reach ~93% amortized utilization with the proposed mixing strategy (steady slots + short bursts) but only if we reserve a small hot-pool (5–8 GPUs) for extremely low-latency flows.

If leadership prefers to avoid the hot-pool, we can still hit utilization targets but will need to contract more burst capacity which bumps committed spend.

Marcus
Senior Manager, Serving Runtime

Attachments: gpu_utilization_trace.zip (zip)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, Amanda Humphrey <amanda.humphrey@amazon.com>, Sara Burns <sara.burns@greentech.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: scaling slots, short-burst plans & token-burn projection

Thank you all — consolidation below and next steps. I turned this into the QBR-ready one-pager (attached qbr_consolidated_decisions.pdf) and pasted the decisions & owners.

Decisions (final):
- Short-burst headroom: APPROVED at 25% for QBR baseline, with a conditional auto-throttle at 1.5x monthly spend. (Owner: Lauren)
- Quantization baseline: q4f16 selected for high-throughput pool. (Owner: Marcus)
- SLO relaxation tolerance: 5% tail-latency window accepted for aggressive batching experiments; will gate widening to 10% only if experiments show no top-end regression. (Owner: Irene)
- Hot-pool: keep a 6-GPU hot-pool for ultra-low-latency flows; this preserves business-critical SLAs at modest utilization cost. (Owner: Marcus & Irene)

Action items:
- Marcus: run a 2-week end-to-end lab experiment validating the 1024+ token tail behavior (start Wed 7/7). Deliverable: short report + recommended guardrails.
- Irene: draft the contractual language for the auto-throttle and procurement timeline; coordinate with procurement and Amanda for potential burst credit terms. (start Tue 7/6)
- Priyom: update the cost model and publish the final slide for the QBR deck. (complete by Thu 7/8)

Amanda — can you confirm whether we can get a short-term burst credit SKU or similar program? Sara — looping you to confirm whether Greentech's production spike on 6/12 (the one in the model) had any unexpected tail effects we should account for.

Drive & docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-capacity-qbr-2027
Notion QBR checklist: https://www.notion.so/redwood/Capacity-Runway-Checklist-2027-07

Thanks —
Priyom
Director, Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr_consolidated_decisions.pdf (pdf)
